domain: Maritime safety / Port State Control - would-be task: for a foreign ship inspected in a Paris MoU port, will the inspection end in detention? (features would be ship particulars, flag, company performance, prior inspection history; publisher is the Paris MoU, an intergovernmental body of 27 maritime authorities incl. all EU/EEA coastal states, secretariat The Hague; its central database THETIS is hosted by EMSA)
prediction_question: Dropped at licence triage before task probing: would a Port State Control inspection of a given ship in the Paris MoU region end in detention? Not probed further because no clean, anonymously accessible, redistributable data channel exists (see rejection_reason).
prediction_time: Not established - the lead was closed at licence/access triage, the cheapest decisive step. The task shape (ship-level next-inspection outcome) would have a clean timing contract (inspection date; outcome recorded at inspection), and prior literature exists on detention prediction, which is why the licence check ran first.
target_definition: Would-be label: inspection ends in detention (ship detained with deficiencies). Measured public-channel evidence shows the freely accessible publications are detention-only and cannot carry this label: the Webb Institute psc-inspection-dataset project (github.com/Webb-Institute/psc-inspection-dataset, read 2026-10-24) parsed 115 monthly Paris MoU detention-list PDFs 2015-2024 into 5,079 detention rows and states 'Detention-only: no clean inspections, so no negative class'.

sources.name: Paris MoU Data Sharing page (bulk inspection data, XML)
sources.access: GATED: 'Any interested party can request an account by completing the Paris MoU Data Request Application Form below, to gain access to the data on offer.' (read in the supported browser 2026-10-24; the form collects personal name, email, organisation type, address and asks about API use). Non-browser clients receive a Dutch 404 page for parismou.org URLs; the old 2021 data-sharing announcement is gone (404 in a real browser too).
sources.licence: No redistribution/redistribution-permission terms stated anywhere on the data-access page; the only published terms are account-use terms: '1. The Paris MoU and EMSA assume no liability... 2. ... will not provide any support... 3. The Paris MoU can retract accounts at her own discretion if the use of an account is evaluated as impairing the data sharing system as such.'

license_evidence: Paris MoU Data Sharing page (https://parismou.org/datasharing-public/, read in the supported browser 2026-10-24): bulk inspection data requires an account application; the page's 'Terms and conditions' cover only liability, support and discretionary account retraction; nothing states permission or prohibition to redistribute the data - unstated redistribution terms.

Independent confirmation: Webb-Institute/psc-inspection-dataset (GitHub, read 2026-10-24): 'Paris MOU and Tokyo MOU records are not redistributed - their source terms restrict reproduction, or leave it unclear.'

measurements.access_measured: parismou.org pages 404 to non-browser clients (web extractor received 'Deze pagina bestaat niet' for the announcement URL); the live Data Sharing page loads in the supported browser and shows the gated application form (2026-10-24). The anonymous public channel is monthly detention lists (detention-only, no negative class; 5,079 detention rows 2015-2024 per the Webb Institute compilation).
measurements.measured_on: 2026-10-24, browser session; no bulk data was downloaded (no account requested - standing policy: no unsolicited permission requests).

rejection_reason: Class C, closed under the standing triage policy. Decisive evidence: (1) the only machine-readable bulk channel for inspection outcomes requires an account application (personal + organisation details) - no anonymous channel; (2) the publisher states no redistribution terms for the bulk data (only liability/support/account-retraction terms), so redistribution permission is unstated - not publishable under our rules and not assumable; (3) the only anonymous channel (monthly detention lists) carries detentions only, so the prediction task has no negative class. Would reopen if: the publisher states open redistribution terms for the bulk feed, or publishes outcomes with clean inspections anonymously, or the operator explicitly records a candidate-specific decision to apply for an account and accept the terms (which would then be a recorded operator risk acceptance, never a publisher grant).
review: A measured rejection that saves construction: the task is real and studied in the literature, but no clean public channel exists; the closest public source (USCG PSIX, CC0, used by the Webb Institute project) is a US federal source and outside this tick's EU/EEA regional focus - recorded here so a future non-EU tick can consider the USCG route without re-probing Paris MoU.
next_action: Closed. Reopen conditions in rejection_reason. If a future tick wants the ship-detention task from an open source, start from USCG PSIX (CC0) rather than Paris MoU.

jurisdiction.publisher: Paris Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control (secretariat, The Hague; THETIS database hosted by the European Maritime Safety Agency)

licence_note: Unstated redistribution terms on the gated bulk channel; account-use terms only. No grant exists; nothing was requested.
